quick: OA 30-60 mg OD; gout 120 mg OD
summary: Etoricoxib is a selective COX-2 inhibitor used for osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and acute gout. Lower GI ulcer risk than non-selective NSAIDs but carries cardiovascular and renal cautions. Not FDA-approved; dosing per EMA/standard references.
indications: Relief of pain and inflammation of acute gouty arthritis
Short-term management of acute musculoskeletal/postoperative dental pain (where approved)

dosage.d: 30 mg once daily; may increase to 60 mg once daily

admin: Take once daily, with or without food (onset faster on empty stomach)
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Limit 120 mg gout dose to no more than 8 days
Ensure blood pressure is controlled before and during therapy
Reassess need periodically in chronic use
moa: Selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis at sites of inflammation, producing anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic effects while largely sparing COX-1-mediated gastric mucosal and platelet function at therapeutic doses.

absolute: Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding
Established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease

preg: Contraindicated. NSAIDs in the third trimester risk premature ductus arteriosus closure and oligohydramnios; avoid throughout pregnancy.
lact: Not recommended; excretion in human milk unknown. Avoid during breastfeeding.
renal: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min). Use caution and monitor in mild-moderate impairment, dehydration, or with diuretics/ACE inhibitors due to risk of renal decompensation.
hepatic: Mild impairment (Child-Pugh 5-6): max 60 mg once daily. Moderate impairment (Child-Pugh 7-9): max 60 mg every other day or 30 mg once daily. Contraindicated in severe impairment (Child-Pugh >=10).

major: Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI and renal toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors / ARBs / diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and renal impairment
interactions.food: May take without regard to food; food delays onset.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate liver enzymes, increase blood pressure and reduce renal function.

monitoring: Blood pressure before and regularly during treatment
Renal function, especially in at-risk patients
Edema/weight in cardiac or renal disease
counsel: Take once daily; use lowest dose for shortest time
Report black stools, vomiting blood or severe abdominal pain
Report chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or slurred speech
Monitor for swelling and rising blood pressure
Avoid combining with other NSAIDs and limit alcohol
pk: Store at 20-25 C, protect from moisture
pearls: Lower GI ulcer risk than non-selective NSAIDs, but CV/renal cautions remain
Limit acute gout dose (120 mg) to 8 days maximum
Contraindicated in uncontrolled HTN and established CV disease
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it; do not double the dose.
overdose: Acute overdose may cause GI symptoms, drowsiness, hypertension, renal impairment and respiratory depression. No specific antidote; treat with supportive care, gastric decontamination if early. Not removed by hemodialysis.
